hierarchy: H1 unconditional / H2 acoustic envelope / H3 transient / H4 Reynolds-not-Mach

points.role: same-session control at the declared operating point
halve the driving force: lower Ma and lower Re
double the driving force: Ma 0.125, above the WCSPH limit
key control: Ma raised at the certified Re, only c_s changed
confounder control: same point with t_end doubled
bracket the break: 1.5x the driving force, Ma still below 0.1
high Ma, short accumulated time: a hard Ma cliff would fail here

verdict.statement: Neither Ma alone nor Re alone explains the pattern. At the certified Re ~12.3 the mirrored-wall solution is clean at Ma 0.122 for t_end = 0.6 s (profile rms 0.64 %), and at Ma 0.061 / 0.123 for t_end = 1.0 s (rms 1.23 % / 1.25 %), but degrades at Ma 0.126 by t_end = 2.0 s (rms 4.57 %, wall shear 11.6 %, steady drift 0.053): there is no instantaneous Ma cliff. At fixed t_end = 1.0 s, raising Ma to 0.123 at the certified Re leaves the band intact (rms 1.25 %), while the higher-Re point (Re 23.3, Ma 0.125) fails -- so a pure Reynolds limit (H4) is excluded as well. What does separate every point is the accumulated-time index Psi = Ma * u_max t_end / dx (pass at Psi <= 20.3, fail at Psi >= 32.6, 1.6x margin); Psi is a *post-hoc* correlation over 7 points and is not a validated criterion. The declared operating point of the anchor sits at Psi = 9.0, 3.6x inside the observed break.
verdict.open_item: Two candidates survive and are not separated by the present sweep: (i) Ma-dependent growth of particle disorder, (ii) the doubled dt that comes with the lowered c_s (P3/P4 run at dt = 3.25e-4 vs 1.63e-4 for P0). The discriminating run is c_s = 20 with t_end = 2.0 (twenty-three thousand steps, ~160 s), which does not fit the 120 s local execution cap; a cluster submission sat queued >30 min without dispatch and was abandoned. Until that run exists, the Psi index must not be quoted as a stability criterion.

certificate_envelope.statement: The anchor's <5 % verdict is valid at its declared operating point; extrapolating it to flows that are faster, longer-running or closer to the acoustic limit is not covered by this certificate.
